domain_guidance.summary: This domain addresses current and prospective donor research methodologies, accounting for 15.0 percent of the examination content. Candidates are evaluated on fundamental prospect identification techniques, information gathering strategies, and data analysis practices used in professional fundraising environments.

Focusing on securing the gift, this domain accounts for 22.0 percent of the test. Test takers must demonstrate proficiency in executing solicitation strategies, developing compelling fundraising appeals, closing charitable contributions, and handling formal gift negotiations effectively.

This domain centers on relationship building and stewardship practices, representing 29.0 percent of the overall examination. Candidates are assessed on cultivating sustainable relationships with prospective and current donors, maintaining constituent communication, and implementing effective recognition initiatives.

Covering volunteer involvement, this domain represents 6.0 percent of the total exam material. Study efforts should concentrate on identifying, recruiting, orienting, and managing volunteers who participate in organizational development, governance duties, and fundraising campaigns.

Encompassing leadership and management principles, this domain constitutes 18.0 percent of the evaluation. Candidates are tested on strategic planning, organizational governance, financial management, operational coordination, and supervisory leadership necessary to guide successful fundraising programs.

This domain evaluates ethics, accountability, and professionalism, comprising 10.0 percent of the certification examination. Candidates must understand ethical standards, adhere to professional codes of conduct, practice transparent accountability, and uphold integrity across all fundraising activities.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Candidates should manage their pacing carefully to complete all 200 questions within the allotted 240 minutes. Arrive prepared, remain focused across every domain, and plan your time effectively during the appointment.

faq.answer_text: The CFRE Certified Fund Raising Executive examination contains a total of 200 questions. These questions are distributed across the six defined practice domains according to their specific percentage weights established by CFRE International.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: To successfully pass the CFRE Certified Fund Raising Executive examination, candidates must achieve a scaled score of 500 or above. Performance is evaluated against the established criteria across all six testing domains.

Candidates are allocated a total testing duration of 240 minutes to complete the examination. This time allows test takers to review and respond to all 200 questions presented during the testing appointment.

This certification is administered and issued by CFRE International, which maintains the official exam guide and testing requirements. Check with CFRE International for the current certification path.

editorial.overview: The CFRE Certified Fund Raising Executive exam is administered by CFRE International to evaluate initial knowledge and professional competence in fundraising practice. The assessment covers six distinct domains: Current and Prospective Donor Research, Securing the Gift, Relationship Building, Volunteer Involvement, Leadership and Management, and Ethics, Accountability, and Professionalism across 200 total questions.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Begin preparation by reviewing the official exam guide provided by CFRE International. Candidates should structure study sessions around the six designated domains in accordance with their respective percentage weights. Allocate planned study time to master donor research, gift solicitation, constituent relationships, leadership responsibilities, volunteer management, and ethical professional standards.
editorial.who_should_take: Fundraising professionals with practical experience seeking formal validation of their expertise across six core practice domains should consider this credential. Candidates should review eligibility requirements and guidelines directly with CFRE International.
